candidates.change_summary: Replace assignment to owner with a no-op (commented out) so transferOwnership does not change owner.
Assign owner to msg.sender instead of newOwner so owner is set to caller rather than provided address.
Assign owner to tx.origin instead of newOwner so owner becomes the original transaction sender rather than the provided address.
Invert the require so only non-owners can call guarded functions, changing who can call transferOwnership.
Remove the require so modifier no longer enforces ownership, allowing anyone to call transferOwnership.
Insert assignment to owner inside owned(), changing state so that after calling owned() the owner value is different.

Replace require check in onlyOwner modifier to inverted check so non-owners become allowed and owner remains unchanged after owned() only if caller is owner; this changes whether owned() can be executed and thus whether state changes happen.
Insert assignment to owner inside onlyOwner modifier so any call passing the check will change owner before function body executes.

Delete the require check in onlyOwner modifier so owned() can be called by anyone, potentially changing owner via other mutations or exposures; this allows external callers to invoke owned() and observe differences if owned() mutates state (originally prevented).
Replace the body so transferOwnership assigns owner unconditionally to address(0) instead of newOwner, changing post-call owner.
Replace the body so transferOwnership does nothing (removes the assignment), leaving owner unchanged after call.
Replace onlyOwner modifier body to remove the require, allowing anyone to call transferOwnership and thus change ownership.
Replace the body so transferOwnership assigns owner to msg.sender instead of newOwner, causing different resulting owner.
